1  NC: 2024:KHC-K:5413  MFA No. 200798 of 2022  THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT PAYABLE TO HIM BY SUITABLY MODIFYING THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 23.07.2021 PASSED BY THE HON'BLE IV ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT-XV, VIJAYAPURA, IN MVC NO.845/2017.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE UMESH M ADIGA  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE UMESH M ADIGA) This is a claimant's appeal in M.V.C.No.845 of 2017 on the file of the IV Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-XV, Vijayapura (hereinafter for short referred to as 'Tribunal') against judgment and award passed in the said case dated 23.07.2021, claiming for enhancement of compensation.
2. The matter is posted for admission and with consent of both side advocates', case is taken up for final disposal.
The parties will be referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for sake of convenience.

4. It is the case of the petitioner that on 10.12.2016 around 12.55 p.m., petitioner along with one Prakash Sharanappa @ Gangappa Badiger were going on the motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-32-EG-5187.
Petitioner was riding the said motorcycle and Prakash was pillion-rider.
He met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of the Cab bearing Registration No.KA- 24-2124 by its driver.
As a result of which, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
He has further contended that the petitioner was aged about 45 years.
He was a Coolie and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries, he has been suffering from permanent disability.
With these reasons, he has prayed to award the compensation of Rs.21,50,000/-.
5. The Respondent No.2 - Insurer disputed the contents of the claim petition and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

From the rival contentions of both the parties, the Tribunal had framed the necessary issues for its determination.
7. This matter was clubbed along with M.V.C.No.846 of 2017 and common evidence was recorded.
Petitioners have examined PWs-1 to 4 and got marked Exs.P1 to 29 and closed their evidence.

The respondents have not lead any evidence but got marked Ex.R1.
8.

After hearing both the parties and appreciating the evidence available on record, the Tribunal disposed of the case by the impugned judgment and award dated 23.07.2021.
9.

The Tribunal assessed the income of the claimant as Rs.8,750/- per month, assessed disability at 10%, applied multiplier as '14' and assessed the compensation towards loss of dependency and in all,
the NC: 2024:KHC-K:5413 Tribunal has awarded the following amount of compensation:
Sl. Heads of Compensation Amount No. (in Rs.) 1 Injury, pain and suffering 30,000 2 Loss of earning capacity on 1,47,000 account of permanent physical disability 3
Medical expenses 3,73,956 4

Future medical expenses 50,000 5 Food, nourishment,
special 5,000 diet and incidental charges 6 Attendant and conveyance 15,000 7 Loss of amenities 10,000 8 Loss of income during laid 26,250 up period Total 6,57,206 Rounded off to 6,57,300 10.
The appellant has challenged the same on the ground of inadequacy of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

11. Heard the learned counsel for the claimant and learned counsel for Respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
12.
Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the Tribunal had not considered disability properly.
According to PW-3, petitioner has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 30 to 34%.
Further, the Tribunal had considered it as 10%.

No amount of compensation is awarded towards future medical expenses though PW-3 has stated that petitioner requires another surgery to remove the implants and the amount of compensation under the other heads are also meager.
Therefore, he prayed for enhancement of compensation.
13. Learned counsel for Respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and submitted that there is no reason to interfere with the same.
14. The Tribunal has considered the evidence of PW-3 and rightly held that the petitioner has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 10%.
It does not call for any interference.
However, out of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, except the medical expenses and future medical expenses, the amount awarded under other heads reconsideration is required.
The petitioner has sustained fracture of proximal tibia and NC: 2024:KHC-K:5413 fibula right and left Iranna S/O Sanganna Pattar vs Hanamantray S/O Gollalappa Karagond ...

3 clavicle.
He underwent surgery in Higher Medical Centre at Miraj on 30.01.2017, 02.02.2017 and 14.02.2017.
Prior to that, he underwent treatment in Basanagouda Memorial Hospital, Vijayapura.
He was admitted as an inpatient at Vijayapura for 32 days and in the hospital at Miraj for 22 days.
15. PW-4 in his evidence has stated that petitioner has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 60% to the right lower limb.
In the cross-examination, PW-4 says that petitioner is a Goldsmith and he used to work by sitting.
He also says that there is reduction in the length right leg to an extent of 6 centimeters and he has also stated that he had not measured both the legs.
16. The learned counsel for Respondent No.2 submits that the fractures are healed and there is no reference regarding maluniting of the fracture.
Therefore, it needs to be considered as fracture united.
The petitioner sustained fracture of all the three bones of the right leg; the reduction of length of the right leg.
He is said to be a NC: 2024:KHC-K:5413 Goldsmith and he has to sit and do his work.
In the examination-in-chief, PW-4 says that petitioner limps while walking.
There is stiffness in the right knee; squatting and sitting cross-legged is not possible at all.
Considering the said facts, the Tribunal ought to have taken disability at 1/3rd of 60% instead of 10% to the whole body.
17. For about 52 days, appellant was admitted as an inpatient.

Looking to the nature of the injuries,
it does not appear that atleast for a period of six months, he is in a position to attend to his duties.
The petitioner had taken treatment at Miraj for 22 days as inpatient.

As per the evidence of PW-4,
he has taken follow-up treatment and also taken physiotherapy.

Considering all these facts,
compensation has to be enhanced under the above said heads.
Accordingly, following amount of compensation is awarded:
Sl . Heads
of Compensation Amount No. (in Rs.)
1 Pain and suffering 75,000 2 Loss of future earning 2,94,000 capacity due to permanent NC: 2024:KHC-K:5413 disability (Rs.8750X12X14X20%) 3
Medical expenses 3,73,956 4
Future medical expenses 50,000 5
Special diet and 30,000 nourishment 6 Attendant charges and 30,000 conveyance charges 7 Loss of amenities 50,000 8 Loss of income during laid 52,500 up period
Total 9,55,456 Less awarded by Tribunal 6,57,300 Enhanced amount 2,98,156
The claimant is entitled for enhancement of Rs.2,98,156/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Ninety Eight Thousand One Hundred and Fifty Six only) with 6% interest from the date of petition till its realization.

18. For the aforesaid discussion, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The impugned judgment and award passed by the IV Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-XV,
